title: Time-bounded composition
statement: Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be finite Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet, let $f$ and $g$ be functions on Boolean words, and let $T_1,T_2$ be functions from natural numbers to natural numbers. Suppose $M_1$ computes $f$ in time $T_1$, $M_2$ computes $g$ in time $T_2$, and $T_2$ is monotone. Then there exist a finite Turing machine $M$ and a natural number $c$ such that $M$ computes $g\circ f$ in time $n\mapsto c\bigl(T_1(n)+T_2(T_1(n))+1\bigr)$.
replaced:
Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be multi-tape Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet,
let $f$ and $g$ be functions on Boolean words, and let $T_1, T_2 : \mathbb{N}
\to \mathbb{N}$ with $T_2$ monotone.  Suppose $M_1$ computes $f$ in time $T_1$
and $M_2$ computes $g$ in time $T_2$, meaning that on every input $x$ the
machine halts within $T_i(\abs{x})$ steps with the function value on its
output tape.  Then there exist a machine $M$ and a constant $c$ such that $M$
computes the composite $g \circ f$ in time
$n \mapsto c \cdot \bigl(T_1(n) + T_2(T_1(n)) + 1\bigr)$.
